summary: The blueprint broadly covers healthy human pancreas but needs targeted fixes for a redundant acinar/ductal mirror axis, mural-cell gating, and a few marker/name refinements.

issues.description: This axis is the exact reciprocal of axis:exocrine_acinar_vs_ductal and therefore adds a padded mirror dimension rather than new pancreatic biology.
issues.suggested_fix: Delete axis:ductal_vs_acinar and keep one acinar/ductal contrast axis, or replace the dimension with a non-duplicative exocrine refinement/state axis.

issues.description: The pericyte/smooth-muscle program is gated by a fibroblast/ECM-heavy mesenchymal_matrix module, which can suppress expected pancreatic mural cells that express RGS5, PDGFRB, CSPG4, MCAM, NOTCH3, ACTA2, TAGLN, or MYH11 without strong fibroblast matrix identity.
issues.suggested_fix: Represent mural cells with an ungated plain axis or create a broader stromal/mural gate that includes mural markers, while keeping fibroblast/stellate and myofibroblast programs as separate refinements.

issues.description: The epsilon/ghrelin-cell module is biologically thin for healthy human pancreas: GHRL is appropriate, but MLN is more typical of intestinal enteroendocrine motilin cells, and SLC18A2 and PCSK1 are shared endocrine markers.
issues.suggested_fix: Make this a conservative rare endocrine/ghrelin axis with stronger pancreatic epsilon specificity and remove MLN, or de-emphasize it if focusing on common adult pancreatic cell types.

issues.description: The module name says T/NK, but its markers are essentially T-cell markers, while NK/cytotoxic identity is already handled by nk_cytotoxic_cell.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename or reinterpret this as a T-cell axis, or deliberately broaden the marker set if a combined lymphoid axis is intended; keep NK/cytotoxic cells separated by the existing NK module.

out_of_scope: Disease-specific axes such as acinar-to-ductal metaplasia or activated inflammatory fibrosis are not required for this healthy/baseline scenario, though generic stress axes are reasonable for scRNA-seq state capture.
